The worn, wooden tables and the faint scent of old books transported her to the university's library, where she had spent countless hours pouring over research papers and scribbling notes in the margins. It was a chilly autumn morning when Edrine first stepped onto the campus, her eyes wide with wonder as she took in the imposing façade of the university's main building. The intricate stone carvings and the grand clock tower seemed to whisper secrets of the past, drawing her in with an otherworldly allure. As she made her way to her first lecture, the sound of rustling leaves beneath her feet served as a gentle reminder that she was about to embark on a journey that would change the course of her life. Professor Jānis, her thesis advisor, would often regale her with stories of the university's rich history, of the countless minds that had shaped the world of science and medicine within those very walls. Edrine would listen, entranced, as he spoke of the pioneering work of Latvian physicians and the groundbreaking discoveries that had been made in the very same laboratories where she now worked. As she delved deeper into her research, Edrine found herself drawn to the university's archives, where dusty tomes and yellowed manuscripts held secrets waiting to be unearthed. It was there, surrounded by the whispers of the past, that she stumbled upon an obscure reference to a long-forgotten study on the very topic she was investigating. The thrill of discovery still lingered in her mind, a spark that had ignited a fire within her to uncover the truth. Now, as she sat in the café, Edrine's thoughts were interrupted by the sound of laughter and the clinking of cups. She looked up to see a group of students, their faces aglow with excitement, gathered around a table near the window. They were discussing their own research projects, their words tumbling out in a rapid-fire sequence as they debated the merits of various methodologies. Edrine smiled, recognizing the same fervor that had driven her own research. She knew that she had been in their shoes not so long ago, and that Riga Stradiņš University had been the catalyst for it all.
